query: Consider the following context: Melting properties are critical for designing novel materials, especially for discovering high-performance, high-melting refractory materials. Experimental measurements of these properties are extremely challenging due to their high melting temperatures. Complementary theoretical predictions are, therefore, indispensable. One of the most accurate approaches for this purpose is the ab initio free-energy approach based on density functional theory (DFT). However, it generally involves expensive thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular dynamic simulations. The high computational cost makes high-throughput calculations infeasible. In that context, which method can be used for calculate its melting properties, including the melting temperature, entropy and enthalpy of fusion, and volume change at the melting point, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Machine Learning Potentials (MLPs) can be used to calculate the melting properties of novel refractory materials, including melting temperature, entropy and enthalpy of fusion, and volume change at the melting point, with reduced computational cost compared to the ab initio free-energy approach based on density functional theory (DFT).
generation.intervention: Application of Machine Learning Potentials (MLPs) to calculate melting properties
generation.mechanism: Reducing the computational cost of thermodynamic integration using machine learning algorithms to fit potential energy surfaces
generation.predicted_outcome: Accurate calculation of melting properties with reduced computational cost
generation.baseline: Ab initio free-energy approach based on density functional theory (DFT)
generation.boundary: High melting temperatures, limited computational resources
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the accuracy of MLPs for high-temperature properties, potential limitations in transferability to new materials

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of melting properties calculated using MLPs and ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT for a set of novel refractory materials
measurements: Volume change at the melting point
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the difference in calculated melting properties between MLPs and ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT is greater than 10%, or if the computational cost reduction is less than 50%, the hypothesis is falsified
